Subject: Initial MAP draft + ask: AWS Private Offer + billing flow

Irene / Redwood team — thanks again for the demo last week. Emerald Systems is ready to formalize next steps for a pilot and have our procurement/legal teams align on an AWS Private Offer path. Attached is a quick mutual-action-plan (Emerald_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short scope summary (Emerald_SOW_summary.pdf).

High level asks from our side:
- We prefer an AWS Private Offer (PO routed through AWS). Can Redwood confirm whether invoices will be sent via AWS or directly from Redwood if required?
- Target pilot: 3 months, ~250k tokens/day sustained; start window: Nov 15–Dec 1.
- Billing terms: Emerald prefers Net 30 and a single consolidated invoice if routed through AWS marketplace billing.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence + standard IP/data use language (we attached a checklist).

Can you propose a short MAP (milestones, owners, dates) that lines up legal, procurement, technical acceptance, and invoicing? We need a recommended close-by date to include in our internal approval packet (finance review on Oct 20).

Thanks — Mark

Thanks Mark — appreciate the packet. Quick confirmation and proposed MAP below. I've looped Jonas (marketplace ops) and Grace (legal/finance) to cover billing and contract items.

Summary answers up front:
- AWS Private Offer billing: Redwood supports the standard AWS Private Offer flow where AWS issues the customer invoice; Redwood receives payment via AWS. If Emerald needs Redwood to invoice directly for any portion (rare), we can support that via an amendment — we'll identify that explicitly in the PO terms.
- Net 30: OK (we'll reflect in the PO metadata); need Emerald's billing entity and PO template.

Proposed Mutual Action Schematic (short):
1) Legal review & PO readiness (owner: Grace) — deliverable: PO template + redlines returned (due: 2026-10-12)
2) AWS Private Offer draft (owner: Jonas) — deliverable: private-offer link & pricing table (due: 2026-10-14)
3) Technical acceptance criteria & pilot plan (owner: Irene) — deliverable: acceptance checklist & test dataset (due: 2026-10-18)
4) Procurement signoff & finance approval (owner: Emerald procurement) — deliverable: signed PO and HubSpot deal updated (target: 2026-10-20)
5) PO execution & AWS Private Offer activation (owner: Jonas/Redwood ops) — deliverable: AWS PO accepted, private offer active (target: 2026-10-25)
6) Pilot kickoff (owner: Irene/Emerald technical lead) — deliverable: pilot kickoff notes & monitoring dashboard (target window: 2026-11-15 to 2026-12-01)

I attached a one-page draft (I put the MAP entries into the spreadsheet you sent) and a short AWS-private-offer checklist (aws-private-offer-draft.iam).

Next steps I propose: 30-min sync this week to confirm legal redlines and clarify billing flow. Jonas — can you confirm the process and whether any additional paperwork is needed for consolidated invoicing? Grace — can you scope redline turn-time if Emerald returns a standard PO by Oct 8?

Best,

Irene / Mark — quick ops note on AWS Private Offer flow and invoice consolidation:

- Standard: Customer (Emerald) accepts the Private Offer; AWS will include the charge on Emerald's AWS invoice. Payment flows through AWS; Redwood reconciles via AWS settlement reports.
- Consolidated invoice: If Emerald wants a single consolidated line for Redwood charges across multiple regions, we can request that via the AWS Marketplace setup, but final formatting is controlled by AWS billing.
- PO metadata: Please include the customer billing entity name, billing address, tax ID (if applicable), and PO number in the Private Offer acceptance. That ensures automated matching.

Operational blockers to highlight:
- If Emerald requires Redwood to issue vendor invoices (instead of AWS), we'll need treasury approval and a short SOW amendment — that adds ~5 business days.
- For SOC2 artifacts: Grace, can we provide the SOC2/attestation doc and a short description of retention controls by Oct 9?

Irene — earliest I can create the private-offer draft is Oct 12 (after we have confirmed final pricing and PO metadata). If Emerald can return PO template by Oct 8 as requested, we can hit the Oct 25 activation target.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Marketplace Operations
jonas_weber@redwood.com

If Emerald confirms PO template delivery by EOD Oct 8, we are aligned to meet these dates. Otherwise, each 1-week slip on PO turnaround shifts activation ~1 week.
